scenes.audio: Aisha sees an online post promising that a life policy is a risk-free savings account with guaranteed large returns.
scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.visual: Static digital frame on cream background with teal header. Three rectangular cards appear sequentially: white, teal, and white. Black and gold circular logo in lower left. No human subjects. Clean, flat digital lighting.

scenes.audio: A polished design does not make that description accurate. Maryland prohibits untrue, deceptive, or misleading insurance advertising and misleading policy descriptions.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Continuation of previous frame. All cards now visible. Palette is teal, white, and dark grey. Minimalist graphic design. No camera movement.

scenes.audio: Identify the product as life insurance, explain material conditions, and separate guarantees from assumptions.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Graphic remains static. Cards are sequentially highlighted with thin teal borders to emphasize spoken points. Minimalist aesthetic on cream backdrop.

scenes.audio: The same honesty belongs in a conversation, a social post, and a presentation. An attractive result based on a possible future crediting rate should never be presented as a contractual promise.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: Static presentation slide. Neutral cream background with teal and dark grey text elements. No subject movement or transitions.

scenes.audio: An illustration can project guaranteed and nonguaranteed policy values over time. The labels matter.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: New slide appears. Cream background with teal header. Three distinct boxes: white, teal, and white. Clean digital layout with gold logo in corner.

scenes.audio: Maryland requires the applicable guaranteed elements to appear before corresponding nonguaranteed elements.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Graphic focuses on the central teal box. Static camera. Flat digital lighting across the text-based interface.

scenes.audio: Nonguaranteed assumptions can change, and actual results can be higher or lower.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Static view of the three informational cards. Minimalist design continues with balanced color palette of teal and white.

scenes.audio: Suppose a projected dividend is expected to help pay a future premium. That projection does not make the policy paid up.
scenes.label: Problem Solving
scenes.visual: Graphic remains static. Visual focus shifts through narrative only. Cream and teal aesthetic remains consistent.

scenes.audio: The rules prohibit misleading vanishing premium language when it implies that nonguaranteed values eliminate the continuing obligation. Show what happens if the assumed results do not occur.
scenes.label: Problem Solving
scenes.visual: The third card on the right is highlighted with a teal outline. Static digital presentation with no environmental detail.

scenes.audio: If a policy is applied for as illustrated, the signed basic illustration goes to the insurer with the application, and a copy goes to the applicant. If the insurer issues different terms, a revised illustration must match the issued policy.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: Transition to third slide. Three cards: white, dark grey, and white connected by teal arrows. Arrows animate from left to right to show process flow.

scenes.audio: It is labeled revised, and signed and dated no later than delivery, with copies for the insurer and policy owner. Do not keep showing a more attractive old version. If no conforming illustration was used at application, follow the certification and delivery procedure required for that situation.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: Central dark grey box and final white box highlighted sequentially. Graphic maintains high-contrast professional design.

scenes.audio: The buyer's guide gives general help with understanding and comparing life insurance. A policy summary supplies the specified costs and guaranteed benefits of the particular policy.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Fourth slide transition. Teal header with three boxes: white, teal, white. Symmetrical layout on cream background.

scenes.audio: An illustration has its own rules for depicting values over time. Maryland generally requires the buyer's guide before acceptance of the initial premium.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Highlighting shifts to the third card on the right. Static digital frame. Gold circular logo visible in corner.

scenes.audio: If the policy has an unconditional refund provision of at least ten days, the guide may instead arrive with or before policy delivery. For covered forms not marketed with an illustration, the required policy summary follows the same delivery timing.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Visual remains static on the current slide cards. Clean, corporate design with flat lighting.

scenes.audio: Elena collects income and other private information for a life application. That does not make the information available for any marketing purpose.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: Fifth slide transition. Four numbered horizontal rows appear, alternating teal and white. Narrative mentions 'Elena' but no human figure is shown.

scenes.audio: Maryland's financial privacy rules generally require a clear initial notice when the customer relationship starts. Before certain disclosures to a nonaffiliated third party, the licensee must provide the required notices and a reasonable opportunity to opt out.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: Rows 1, 2, and 4 are highlighted sequentially with borders as mentioned. Graphic aesthetic remains minimalist and text-heavy.

scenes.audio: The customer must not have opted out. Exceptions exist for specified transaction servicing and other lawful purposes.
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: Static view of the four privacy-related rows. Uniform cream background with digital logo in corner.

scenes.audio: Identify the information, recipient, and purpose before deciding which rule applies. Annual privacy notices are generally part of a continuing customer relationship.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Sixth slide transition. Title banner at top. Three rectangular boxes in white, teal, and white layout. Static digital view.

scenes.audio: But Maryland has an exception when disclosures are limited to the specified permitted categories and the disclosed policies and practices have not changed. Non-public health information has a separate authorization rule with listed insurance function exceptions, including underwriting and claims work.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: The central teal box is highlighted. Frame remains static with high-contrast text for legibility.

scenes.audio: That matters even in a life insurance application. An exception for a real underwriting task is not permission to post a client's diagnosis in a sales chat. Use approved systems, limit access, and preserve the required records.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: Highlight moves to the final white box on the right. Slide ends on this frame with circular gold and black logo clearly visible.
